Article Title: Your loan EMI has a Washington problem: How the Fed quietly influences RBI rate decisions
Article Text:
When the US Fed hikes rates, dollar assets such as US Treasuries become more attractive. (Image for representative purpose only)

What does this mean for your EMI? How does the US Federal Reserve’s decision tighten the situation for RBI? Let’s decode:

What US Fed has done and what it means for India

Rising inflation: Is a rate hike inevitable?

Brent crude prices since the US-Iran war began

What a rate hike would mean for your EMI

25 & 50 bps rate hike scenario for a Rs 50 lakh loan at 7.25% for 25 years

Last Wednesday, the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since July 2023. Thousands of miles away, sitting in your home which you have bought on loan, your EMI may take a hit.The US Federal Reserve’s quarter-percentage-point rate hike has added to the challenges facing the RBI ahead of its monetary policy review in October.“Global growth is projected to soften while inflation forecast is higher for 2026 vis a vis the previous year. Some central banks have tightened policy, while others remain vigilant. Crude oil prices, currencies and financial markets remain volatile, fluctuating in line with the changing intensity and uncertainties of the West Asia conflict,” RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra had said in the August review statement by the Monetary Policy Committee.Almost two months later, inflationary pressures on the economy have increased. And the US Fed’s rate hike signals tighter monetary conditions. RBI has the balancing act of reducing inflation without compromising on growth channels. With inflation rising and GDP growth beating estimates, experts see a rate hike by the central bank as a prudent move.Last week, the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates by 25 basis points and another rate hike has been forecast by the end of this year.This sent US bond yields up. The reason was simple: inflation in the US is persistently high and tariffs and oil prices are adding to a cloudier outlook.But, why should the US Fed rate math make any difference to your loan EMI?The cycle works like this: When the US Fed hikes rates, dollar assets such as US Treasuries become more attractive. This can lead to capital outflows from India which in turn puts pressure on the rupee.A weaker and depreciating rupee makes imports expensive. And in India’s case there is double whammy: it imports around 90% of its crude needs and oil prices are currently rising globally due to the US-Iran conflict. Add to that a weaker rupee and the import bill suddenly goes up, adding to input cost pressures and potentially triggering higher inflation. Higher import costs can feed into transport, manufacturing and eventually household prices.RBI does not have to follow the Fed. It sets policy according to Indian inflation and growth. But currency weakness and imported inflation can reduce its room to cut rates - or strengthen the argument for keeping rates elevated. Forex intervention can soften currency swings, without eliminating the underlying pressures.If inflation moves beyond RBI’s comfort zone, it then hikes repo rate to keep it under check. Repo rate is the rate at which the central bank lends to the RBI. If that goes up, banks in turn hike loan rates since the higher cost of borrowing for banks makes way to higher cost of lending.If RBI raises its repo rate, repo-linked floating home loans would typically become costlier when rates reset.Most economists and experts expect the RBI to hike repo rate this year, if not in the October policy, then in the December one. But a wait-and-watch approach is likely.The RBI looks to maintain retail inflation in the 2-6% range, with 4% as the target. Some economists see the 6% number being breached in the coming months. Retail inflation is already inching to 5% levels while WPI is nearing double-digit numbers.In a recent report SBI Research said that CPI inflation may cross-6.5% mark before dropping to less than 6% in early 2027.“Time to build moats through a 25-bps hike in October and Dec MPC each, and then to pause and take stock with upcoming data!” SBI said in its report.Global crude oil prices are hovering near $100, and a weaker rupee and tighter global financial conditions due to the US Fed rate hike will all add to the pressure on inflation.DK Srivastava, Chief Policy Advisor, EY India explains why the case for a rate hike has strengthened.“Recent trends in WPI and CPI indices indicate persistent pressure on inflation. This inflation is primarily due to cost push and supply side factors. These include the impact of El Nino linked deficient monsoon and rising crude oil prices. These have resulted in higher food prices,” he tells TOI.Alongside, there is also a relatively high growth of money supply. Average growth in M3 was 15.0% during June to August 2026.According to Srivastava, the RBI is likely to take into account the following factors in determining its policy stance and rate: recent US Fed rate hike by 25 basis points, comfortable growth situation with first quarter real GDP growth in FY27 at 7.8%, persistent increase in WPI and CPI inflation in recent months, and sustained increase in M3 growth above trend.“Chances for a change in the policy stance and a 25 basis points hike in the repo rate are high in the October 2026 MPC meeting,” he says.According to Ranen Banerjee, Partner and Leader, Economic Advisory, PwC, RBI will watch for the reaction to the US Federal Reserve hike in terms of outflows and pressure on the currency.“A repo rate hike is inevitable, but may not happen in the October review. The MPC may choose to wait and watch for inflation trajectory since the number is still within the target range and then opt for a hike in its December policy review if inflationary and fund outflow pressures do not abate and high frequency economic indicators continue to print strong,” Banerjee tells TOI.Depending on the loan terms, a repo rate hike would mean that your EMI could rise, your repayment period could lengthen, or both.Even without a hike, the rate relief borrowers hoped for could move further away, and that too ahead of the festive season if the MPC goes in for a repo rate increase on October 7.Adhil Shetty, CEO, Bankbazaar.com explains the scenarios: A 25 basis point repo rate hike does not mean every home-loan EMI will rise by the same amount. The impact depends on the loan benchmark, reset cycle and whether the full rate increase is passed on.“External benchmark-linked loans, including repo-linked loans, generally reflect changes in the benchmark more directly, while MCLR-linked loans follow the reset cycle in the loan agreement,” he tells TOI.For example, at 7.5%, the EMI on a Rs 40 lakh loan with 25 years remaining is about Rs 29,560. If the rate rises by 25 basis points to 7.75%, the EMI would increase to about Rs 30,210, assuming the full increase is passed on and the tenure remains unchanged. A 50 basis point increase to 8% would take it to about Rs 30,870.“Borrowers should check their benchmark and reset terms to understand the actual impact on their EMI and tenure,” he advises.
Article Summary: US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since July 2023. When the US Fed hikes rates, dollar assets such as US Treasuries become more attractive. This can lead to capital outflows from India which in turn puts pressure on the rupee. A weaker and depreciating rupee makes imports expensive.

Article Title: Banks to open on Sunday ahead of 3-day nationwide strike: What customers should know
Article Text:
The government said it has taken the proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens. (AI image)

Also read:

Why are bank unions planning a strike?

NEW DELHI: Banks will remain open on Sunday, September 27, to ensure customers have access to essential banking services ahead of a proposed three-day nationwide strike, the government said on Wednesday.The move comes after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With September 26 and 27 falling on a weekend, the strike could otherwise lead to an extended disruption in banking services, the govt said.“In view of the proposed three-day nationwide bank strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) from September 28 to 30, 2026, coinciding with the preceding weekend holidays of September 26 and 27, the government has taken proactive steps to safeguard the banking needs of citizens,” the finance ministry said in a statement.“In order to ensure that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, all Public Sector Banks and Regional Rural Banks will function normally on Sunday, the 27th of September, 2026,” the ministry said.“The Department reiterates that the welfare and convenience of bank customers remains the Government's foremost priority. The Government and bank managements have appealed to unions to defer the proposed strike, and have also taken measures to ensure that essential banking services continue un-interrupted,” it added.The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests on September 27.“Permission to operate Bank Branches and Currency Chests on Sunday, September 27, 2026. As requested in the above letter, with a view to ensuring that the genuine banking needs of the public are not adversely affected for an extended period, you have our approval for keeping the branches, offices, ATM link branches and Currency Chests of banks fully operational on Sunday, September 27, 2026," the apex bank said.“The banks may be advised to ensure adherence to relevant legal requirements in this regard. A list of Currency Chests of private sector/foreign banks has been sent to you separately,” it added.The UFBU has said bank operations could be disrupted across the country during the three-day strike from September 28 to 30. Since the strike follows the weekend holidays, customers could potentially face an effective five-day disruption in banking services.The timing is also significant as September 30 marks the half-yearly closing of banks, when reconciliation, provisioning, and treasury and market operations are carried out.The UFBU, which claims to represent around 90% of the banking workforce, has said it will proceed with the strike unless there is concrete progress on its key demand for five-day banking.“Responding to the appeal made by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Indian Banks' Association (IBA), Bank managements to defer the strike, we informed them that if there is any concrete and positive development towards implementation of our demand for introduction of 5 days banking, UFBU will consider the same,” the UFBU said in a statement following a meeting with the deputy chief labour commissioner.UFBU's other demands include an update and improvement of pension, a uniform dearness allowance formula for all pensioners and an option for employees covered under the National Pension System (NPS) to move to the old pension scheme (OPS). Bank unions under the UFBU had also gone on a nationwide strike on September 11 over their demands.The statement came after a conciliation meeting on Tuesday ended without a resolution. In the absence of such progress, the union said it would be “constrained” to go ahead with the proposed strike on September 28, 29 and 30.
Article Summary: The move comes after the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) called for a nationwide strike from September 28 to 30. With September 26 and 27 falling on a weekend, the strike could otherwise lead to an extended disruption in banking services. The Reserve Bank of India has also approved the operation of bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent crude eases as Iran keeps door open to diplomacy
Article Text:
Oil prices had slipped below $100 a barrel on Wednesday.

Oil prices edged lower on Thursday after rising about 4% in the previous session, as investors assessed signs that Iran remained open to diplomacy to end its war with the US, although the two sides remain far apart on the terms of a possible agreement.At 7:30 am IST, WTI crude was trading at $91.87 per barrel, down 0.32%, while Brent crude was at $102.53 per barrel, lower by 0.54%.Earlier, Brent crude futures fell 0.9%, to $102.13 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures eased 0.7%, to $91.56.Oil prices had slipped below $100 a barrel on Wednesday after Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supplies through a key pipeline to the Red Sea. Hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran conflict also weighed on prices.Brent had closed below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8.Iran and the US remain divided over how to end the war, but diplomacy must continue, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Wednesday. The comments came after Iran's president told the UN General Assembly that Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.Tehran was reviewing Washington's response to its peace proposals, which prioritise lifting a US naval blockade on Iranian ports and reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the official said.The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and lifting of Washington's naval blockade on Iran were discussed during indirect talks on Tuesday, the official added.However, Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz would not be reopened until Iran's conditions were met.US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a deal with Iran would require hard work over a period of time, while adding that US President Donald Trump also had military options.Traders were also assessing the possibility of restrictions on US diesel exports. Ultra-low-sulfur diesel futures fell about 5% in midday trading after Politico reported that the Trump administration was preparing plans for a 90-day diesel export ban. The White House later denied the report.However, Bloomberg reported, citing sources, that Energy Secretary Chris Wright told oil industry leaders to prepare for possible US curbs on diesel exports during calls late Tuesday.Wright had said earlier on Wednesday that a diesel export ban would not work, even as Trump said he would support such a move.Analysts and market watchers have warned that an export ban would do little to ease high energy prices and could instead tighten global supplies and further disrupt economies.Meanwhile, US crude inventories rose by 3 million barrels to 426.4 million barrels last week, according to the Energy Information Administration.
Article Summary: Oil prices edged lower on Thursday after rising about 4% in the previous session. Investors assessed signs that Iran remained open to diplomacy to end its war with the US. Hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran conflict also weighed on prices. Oil prices had slipped below $100 a barrel on Wednesday.

Article Title: She paid US tax but missed Form 67, triggering Rs 30 lakh India tax demand; ITAT Delhi orders relief, asks AO to verify Rs 23.48 lakh credit claim after 6-year fight
Article Text:
The ITAT Delhi noted that the woman had claimed a foreign tax credit of Rs 23.48 lakh in her ITR. (Image for representative purpose)

What the case is about

How did the woman win the case in ITAT Delhi?

You are an Indian-origin US citizen and you pay your taxes in America. But a tax demand for your income is raised in India because of an error on your part. What happens then?In one such case, a woman paid income tax in the US and sought to claim credit for the tax under the India-USA DTAA while filing her taxes in India.Under the applicable rules, taxpayers who have paid taxes in a foreign country with which India has a Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (DTAA) are required to submit Form 67 along with their ITR to claim credit in India for the foreign taxes already paid.The woman failed to file Form 67, a mistake that resulted in the Income Tax Department refusing her foreign tax credit (FTC) claim. The department subsequently raised an income tax demand of Rs 30 lakh against her.She subsequently took steps to have the matter reconsidered. She approached the jurisdictional AO with a rectification application. She also belatedly submitted her Form 67 February 8, 2023, after the prescribed deadline. However both the tax officer and the commissioner of appeals (CIT A) rejected her claims.She then challenged the tax demand before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Delhi.The tribunal ruled in her favour on September 14, 2026.The ITAT Delhi noted that the woman had claimed a foreign tax credit of Rs 23.48 lakh in her ITR, but had not submitted Form 67 along with the return.The form was also not filed before the Income Tax Department processed her return under Section 143(1). Instead, she submitted Form 67 later, on February 8, 2023.By that time, the CPC, Bengaluru had already processed her ITR on March 21, 2020, while rejecting the foreign tax credit claimed by her.Before processing the return, however, the CPC had referred the case to the jurisdictional AO on May 9, 2019. This was because the tax department was unable to verify the credits for taxes paid outside India that she had claimed in her ITR.According to ITAT Delhi, the jurisdictional AO should have initiated proceedings to examine and verify the foreign tax credit claim. However, the material available on record indicated that no such proceedings were commenced by the AO.The tribunal further observed that the records showed no notice under Section 139(8) had been issued by either the AO or CPC before the foreign tax credit was disallowed.Similarly, the Income Tax Department did not issue a notice under the proviso to Section 143(1) before rejecting her claim for the foreign tax credit.Her subsequent rectification application filed under Section 154 was also rejected. Against this backdrop, and in the interest of justice, ITAT Delhi followed the Delhi High Court's ruling in Real Time Data Services (P.) Ltd. v. PCIT, reported in [2026]183 taxmann.com 701 (Delhi).The tribunal directed the AO to allow the foreign tax credit claimed by the woman after carrying out the necessary verification. It also said that if the credit could not be granted for any reason, the AO would have to issue a speaking order explaining the basis for the decision.Karanjot Singh Khurana, Partner, DMD Advocates, told ET that the woman was a citizen of the United States who earned income there and paid tax on that income under US income tax laws.However, during the relevant period, she was a tax resident of India and was therefore liable to tax in India on her global income, including the income she had earned in the USA. Khurana explained that the India-USA tax treaty provides relief from such double taxation by allowing India to provide credit for taxes paid in the USA and tax only the differential amount payable in India. In this case, however, the taxpayer had not filed Form 67, which was required for claiming the foreign tax credit.The Income Tax Department initially turned down her claim for credit of the US taxes because Form 67 had not been filed.According to Khurana, the ITAT Delhi tax tribunal relied on a Delhi High Court ruling in Real Time Data Services (P.) Ltd. v. PCIT, reported in [2026]183 taxmann.com 701 (Delhi). The tribunal held that filing Form 67 is directory rather than mandatory. Consequently, a delay in filing the form, by itself, should not deprive a taxpayer of the right to claim credit for taxes that have already been paid in a foreign country.Khurana explained that a resident taxpayer who wants to claim credit in India for taxes paid or deducted in a foreign country on income that is also taxable in India must file Form 67. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, the corresponding form is Form 44.
Article Summary: The woman paid income tax in the US and sought to claim credit for the tax under the India-USA DTAA while filing her taxes in India. She failed to file Form 67, a mistake that resulted in the Income Tax Department refusing her foreign tax credit (FTC) claim. The department subsequently raised an income tax demand of Rs 30 lakh against her. The tribunal ruled in her favour on September 14, 2026.

Article Title: NSE sees tepid debut; exchange becomes ninth most valued listed company in India at Rs 4.63 lakh crore
Article Text:
Macquarie has started coverage of NSE with an Outperform rating and assigned a target price of Rs 1,965.

NSE share price today

:

NSE market cap

Analysts’ view

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Shares of National Stock Exchange (NSE) made a subdued debut on Thursday, opening at Rs 1,800 per share on the BSE. The listing price saw a premium of less than 1% over the IPO price of Rs 1,785.Before the listing, NSE's valuation at the IPO price of Rs 1,785 per share stood at Rs 4.42 lakh crore. By comparison, the market capitalisation of rival BSE is Rs 1.33 lakh crore.Following the listing, the shares rallied around 3%, and NSE's market capitalisation rose to Rs 4.63 lakh crore. This makes it the ninth-largest listed company in India's stock market. Exchange data showed that NSE has moved ahead of FMCG major HUL and healthcare company Sun Pharmaceuticals.The newly listed exchange is ranked below Reliance Industries, whose market capitalisation stands at Rs 16.77 lakh crore. HDFC Bank follows with Rs 11.25 lakh crore, while Bharti Airtel, ICICI Bank, SBI, TCS, Bajaj Finance and LT also rank ahead of NSE, according to stock exchange data quoted in an ET report.Despite the lacklustre opening, some market participants said the movement in NSE shares during the initial trading sessions could be shaped considerably by the balance between demand and available supply.Restrictions on exits for most large shareholders could keep the immediate supply of shares limited, which may provide support to the stock at a later stage."While GMP indicators hinted at a muted 2-5% premium, the real story lies in its tight initial supply," said Manish Bhandar of Vallum Capital Advisors.Sebi regulations stipulate that shares held before the issue by non-promoter shareholders are subject to a six-month lock-in from the date of IPO allotment, except for certain categories of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs).Macquarie has started coverage of NSE with an Outperform rating and assigned a target price of Rs 1,965. The target represents a potential upside of 10% from the upper end of the IPO price band.The brokerage has described NSE as “The Dominator”, pointing to its leadership in market share and its strong position in the financial markets. It highlighted the exchange's broad range of services, technology infrastructure and deep liquidity, which it said make NSE an important component of India's financialisation and a “lynchpin” of India's financialization.Macquarie also cited NSE's strong network effects, profitability and cash generation as key supports for the business.For the FY26-30E period, the brokerage expects NSE's revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 12%. It said the expansion would be supported by non-transaction revenues and new products, although this would be partly offset by modest market-share losses in cash equities and F&O.“Upside could come from a higher P/N ratio, growing monthly options adoption, and stronger traction in new products.” the brokerage said.Emkay has also started coverage of NSE with a Buy recommendation, setting a Sep-27E target price of Rs 2,050. The target represents an upside of around 15%.The brokerage's bullish assessment is based on three broad factors. The first is the long-term potential of India's capital markets, supported by increasing wealth creation and financialisation. Emkay expects India's per capita GDP to rise from around $3,000 to $10,000 over the coming decades, providing a lengthy growth runway for the country's capital markets.The second factor is NSE's ability to retain its leadership across various capital market segments over the years. Emkay said the exchange's business model has enough flexibility to respond to shifts in regulation and macroeconomic conditions while sustaining profitable growth.The third consideration is the profitability and cash-generating ability of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs), including stock exchanges. According to Emkay, such institutions command higher valuation multiples globally than other capital market businesses because the latter tend to be more fragmented and face greater competitive pressures.Most brokerages covering the IPO had assigned a 'Subscribe' recommendation, although some, including Religare, took a neutral view.NSE's Rs 22,562-crore IPO consisted entirely of an offer for sale (OFS), involving 12.64 crore shares. Since there was no fresh issue component, the exchange itself will not receive any money raised through the IPO. Instead, the proceeds will go to the existing shareholders who sold their stakes. The IPO was priced in the range of Rs 1,700-1,785 per share, with each lot comprising eight shares.Investor demand took the overall subscription level to 5.71 times the shares on offer. The retail portion was subscribed 1.39 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 6.55 times. Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) generated the strongest response, with their reserved portion receiving 12.68 times subscription.
Article Summary: Shares of National Stock Exchange (NSE) made a subdued debut on Thursday, opening at Rs 1,800 per share on the BSE. The listing price saw a premium of less than 1% over the IPO price of Rs1,785. Macquarie has started coverage of NSE with an Outperform rating and assigned a target price of £1,965.

Article Title: Airtel Money plans to list on LSE, looks to raise $800mn
Article Text:
Airtel Money, is preparing for an initial public offering on the London Stock Exchange to raise at least $800 million at an expected valuation of $8 billion to $9 billion.

NEW DELHI: Sunil Bharti Mittal's Airtel Money, a digital financial services platform operating across 13 African markets, has announced its plan to list on the London Stock Exchange (LSE).Sources said the company could raise about $800 million from an initial public offering ( IPO ) and is targeting a valuation of $8 billion to $9 billion - possibly making it one of London's largest listings in recent years.The company, which provides financial services across Africa through a mobile-led model operating on a highly scalable technology stack, said this IPO "would provide the opportunity to invest in one of Africa's largest fintech platforms that is revolutionising digital financial services and enabling financial inclusion for millions.... outlook reflects the resilience of our model and the significant opportunity we continue to unlock across Africa. "AirtelMoney chief executive officer Ian Ferrao said: "A London listing will underpin our next wave of growth. The opportunity ahead of us is substantial and importantly there are many demographic and digital tailwinds within the markets that we serve... We are approaching this from a position of financial strength. The business is debt-free, capital-light and highly cash generative, which is why this offer consists solely of shares sold by existing shareholders and no new capital is being raised. "
Article Summary: Sunil Bharti Mittal's Airtel Money, a digital financial services platform operating across 13 African markets, has announced its plan to list on the London Stock Exchange. The company could raise about $800 million from an initial public offering ( IPO ) and is targeting a valuation of $8 billion to $9 billion.

Article Title: JSW set to enter e-trucks biz, seeks to drive sales
Article Text:
The vehicles, which will sell under the AMPSTAR brand, add to JSW’s auto portfolio that includes a joint venture with MG Motors, its own plans for JSW Motors and talks for buying into Skoda-VW in India.

MUMBAI: Sajjan Jindal's JSW Greentech is entering the crowded commercial vehicles business with electric trucks, hoping to not just create space for itself but also inject momentum into non-diesel space with ambition to sell one lakh units by 2030. While the plant, which will be operational soon, will have a capacity to produce around 15,000 electric buses and trucks annually, this year, it is expecting to notch up sales of around 3,000 electric trucks in a market that saw the industry selling 800 units last year. Some part of the demand may come from the JSW group itself, which uses around 17,000 trucks.The vehicles, which will sell under the AMPSTAR brand, add to JSW's auto portfolio that includes a joint venture with MG Motors, its own plans for JSW Motors and talks for buying into Skoda-VW in India.Jindal said the company is trying to drive action in the electric trucks business but is also conscious of the risks involved. "There will be challenges. Once we jump into the ocean, we will try to swim," he said, adding that the focus is on creating indigenous capabilities with cells being an area of imports from China. He added that R&D is a focus area and the company is hopeful of achieving a breakthrough in cells over the next few years. "Several Indian groups are working on it. In the next five to seven years, there will be some reverse engineering. I am being very practical: let's first catch up with what is happening in China and then we will try for some breakthrough."
Article Summary: Sajjan Jindal's JSW Greentech is entering the crowded commercial vehicles business with electric trucks. The vehicles, which will sell under the AMPSTAR brand, add to JSW’s auto portfolio that includes a joint venture with MG Motors, its own plans for JSW Motors.

Article Title: ADB, OECD, S&P, Fitch raise India's growth projection
Article Text:
Four agencies raise India’s growth projection

NEW DELHI: The Asian Development Bank and OECD, along with ratings agencies S&P and Fitch, joined Moody's in raising India's growth forecast for the current year. ADB and S&P now expect India's GDP to expand by 7% this year, compared with their earlier projection of 6.6%, while Fitch has pegged its estimate at 6.9%. The sharpest revision was by OECD, which projected 7.1% growth this year, compared with 6.3% in its June outlook.The four agencies expect the monetary policy committee to increase rates in the wake of higher inflation reading. The upgrade in projections follows the first quarter GDP estimates released by the statistics ministry, which estimated that the economy expanded 7.8% during April-June, leading to an upward revision by most economists.While raising its projection from 6.4%, Fitch said: "...the Indian economy has shown resilience in the face of shock from the US-Iran war, despite strong terms-of-trade deterioration seen in first half of 2026. Fitch expects growth to moderate over the remainder of the financial year." It predicted a 25 basis points (a quarter of a percentage point) increase in interest rates.S&P said that India is seeing strong consumption growth, along with strong investment momentum."Several factors drove growth to higher levels than we expected in June quarter. These include robust industrial activity, healthy consumption, strong goods exports and acceleration in govt investment. We have consequently upgraded our GDP growth forecast... That said, we expect growth to ease in second half of the fiscal year as tailwinds from GST rationalisation and income tax cuts diminish. Weather-related risks warrant close monitoring. Cumulative rains were 15% below normal till Sept 9, 2026 in the current monsoon season. Agricultural output and food inflation therefore remain key variables to watch."ADB said India's growth is supported by resilient consumption, healthy investment and strong services exports, which are expected to offset the drag from higher energy costs and a weaker monsoon."The economy is projected to grow faster than expected in FY26 as the impact of the Middle East conflict is mitigated by lower supply disruptions than expected due to geographical diversification of energy imports and consumer protection policies," the latest Asian Development Outlook said. Weak monsoon and West Asia related developments are expected to drive inflation.
Article Summary: ADB and S&P now expect India's GDP to expand by 7% this year, compared with their earlier projection of 6.6%. Fitch has pegged its estimate at 6.9%. The sharpest revision was by OECD, which projected 7.1% growth this year.

Article Title: We don't want to compete with customers, may not run airline: Adani Airports CEO
Article Text:
Adani Airports is the second-largest airport operator globally by passenger traffic, according to Bansal

MUMBAI: Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal said the company does not want to compete with its airline customers and has enough opportunities in the airport business, a day after govt said it was examining the pros and cons of allowing airport operators such as Adani Group to run airlines."As airport CEO, I would not like to compete with my own customers. My hands are full," Bansal said at SBI Banking and Economics Conclave. Bansal said the growth opportunity in India's aviation sector was large enough for Adani Airports to focus its bandwidth on expanding its airport operations rather than entering the airline business."India will be the fastest-growing aviation market in the world over the next 10 years and will be among the top two markets," he said. Adani Airports currently handles about 100 million passengers and Bansal said the company expected India's aviation sector to grow substantially over the next two decades. With GDP potentially growing eightfold in 20 years and aviation growing faster than GDP, the sector could expand about tenfold, he said. "If we are able to capture that, we will be number one in the world," Bansal said.Adani Airports is already the second-largest airport operator globally by passenger traffic, according to Bansal. The company operates airports including Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Thiruvananthapuram, Jaipur, Guwahati and Navi Mumbai.Bansal said the company planned to invest about $11 billion in airport infrastructure in India over the next five years.
Article Summary: Adani Airports CEO Arun Bansal says the company does not want to compete with its airline customers. Bansal: India will be the fastest-growing aviation market in the world over the next 10 years. The company operates airports including Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Lucknow.

Article Title: Baba votes against nephew, but Sameer secures Hikal chair
Article Text:
NO TRUCE Sameer Hiremath (left) and Baba Kalyani

MUMBAI: Baba Kalyani voted against his own nephew and lost. Sameer Hiremath, 52, secured the chairmanship of Hikal despite opposition from Bharat Forge's chairman and MD, with public shareholders tipping the balance.The resolution passed narrowly. Of the votes cast, nearly 52% backed Sameer's appointment as CMD, against 48% who opposed. Public shareholders decided the outcome: the Hiremath family delivered 44% of the votes in favour, with public shareholders adding roughly 8%. The Kalyani family accounted for 43% of the votes against, with public shareholders contributing about 5% on that side.With his elevation, Sameer will become the sole Hiremath representative on Hikal's board. His father, Jai Hiremath, the outgoing chairman, and his mother, Sugandha Hiremath, a non-executive director, both will step down on Oct 1.The voting pattern has upset the apple cart for a dispute meant to be cooling, not heating up. A former Supreme Court judge has been mediating the billion-dollar feud between the Hiremaths and Kalyanis over shared assets, including their Hikal shareholdings and parties under mediation typically avoid moves that strain an already fraught relationship further.The Kalyani camp also voted against the adoption of Hikal's FY26 financial statements, Sarangan Suresh's reappointment as executive director and auditors' remuneration. The only resolution it supported was the FY26 dividend.People familiar with the matter said the vote against the FY26 accounts was a surprise.Hikal's board including Amit Kalyani, Baba Kalyani's son and a non-executive director had already approved those accounts. Voting them down at the shareholder level was, in the words of those tracking the dispute, unusual.
Article Summary: Sameer Hiremath, 52, secured the chairmanship of Hikal despite opposition from Bharat Forge's chairman and MD, with public shareholders tipping the balance. Of the votes cast, nearly 52% backed Sameer's appointment as CMD, against 48% who opposed. The voting pattern has upset the apple cart for a dispute meant to be cooling, not heating up.

Article Title: BRICS should work together on transfer pricing: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
Article Text:
BRICS economies must have say in global tax rules as negotiations shape cross-border taxation: FM Sitharaman

NEW DELHI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday urged BRICS nations to share their experiences on treaty interpretation and multilateral negotiations in international taxation, saying global transfer pricing disputes "disproportionately" burden developing countries.India has proposed to set up two new working groups, International Taxation and Transfer Pricing and Revenue Statistics, at a time when international tax rules are being renegotiated, Sitharaman said, addressing the BRICS heads of tax authorities meeting here."The rules of international taxation are being renegotiated. There are several multilateral tax issues, including the UN Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation, under active negotiation. The decisions made in these processes over the next few years will shape cross-border taxation for a generation."BRICS economies, as source jurisdictions, as large developing economies, as countries that have built significant domestic tax capacity from a low base, have a perspective on those negotiations that is essential to their fairness and their durability," Sitharaman said. Agencies
Article Summary: India has proposed to set up two new working groups, International Taxation and Transfer Pricing and Revenue Statistics. The decisions made in these processes over the next few years will shape cross-border taxation for a generation. BRICS economies must have a perspective on those negotiations that is essential to their fairness and their durability.

Article Title: Inflation to stay within band: RBI deputy governor Poonam Gupta
Article Text:
RBI deputy governor Poonam Gupta

MUMBAI: RBI deputy governor Poonam Gupta said that despite multiple shocks, India's inflation is likely to remain within the target band, unlike several advanced economies where inflation is running above target and may require higher interest rates. She also said that there was scope for the rupee to appreciate from current levels as was being anticipated by analysts following the special scheme which attracted over $133 billion from non-resident deposits.Speaking at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave on Wednesday, Gupta said: "Advanced economies are nearly twice the target levels they have set. US was close to 4%. India is entering this crisis much better." She cautioned that countries would respond differently to the shocks, depending on their circumstances.Gupta said India had faced a wider range of shocks than most emerging economies over the past year and a half, including high US tariffs, oil supply disruptions, El Nino and capital outflows linked to the global AI boom. Yet, the economy had emerged "largely unscathed, and perhaps even stronger structurally".India's growth was the highest among its peers, while inflation remained anchored, fiscal consolidation continued and the financial sector had become more resilient, she said. Gupta said India had also fared well during the energy shock despite its dependence on imports. Unlike many other economies, India saw little rationing of supplies, which helped prevent panic and limited the economic cost of the shock.She said India had maintained fiscal prudence instead of trying to stimulate the economy beyond its productive capacity. IMF has projected that India's public debt as a proportion of GDP would decline by 5.6 percentage points between now and 2031, in contrast to most other countries.
Article Summary: RBI deputy governor Poonam Gupta says India's inflation is likely to remain within the target band. She also said that there was scope for the rupee to appreciate from current levels. She cautioned that countries would respond differently to the shocks, depending on their circumstances.

Article Title: N Chandrasekaran's real vote test: Tata Sons AGM, not boardroom
Article Text:
Tata Sons board resolution on Chandrasekaran reappointment invalid, says Tata Trusts

_

MUMBAI: Even as Tata Sons ' board has reappointed N Chandrasekaran for a third five-year term, his position hinges on another vote for his reappointment as a director. The chairmanship itself does not require shareholder approval. But director reappointment does, through an annual general meeting where majority owners will hold sway.Tata Sons has to decide on a new AGM date as the Aug meeting was adjourned for want of quorum. The company has an extension from the Registrar of Companies to hold the AGM by Dec this year.When it does, a circular resolution will go to all six directors, who will have seven days to respond with a 'yes' or 'no'. If Chandrasekaran succeeds in winning reappointment as director, the chairmanship extends to Feb 21, 2032. Failure to do so, and his term at Tata Sons ends immediately.However, the quorum problem that sank the Aug meeting has not gone away. Tata Sons' Articles of Association require a joint nominee from controlling shareholders, Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and Sir Ratan Tata Trust, as part of the five-shareholder quorum (the other four can be nominees of minority shareholder groups such as the Tata group companies, Shapoorji Pallonji, members of the Tata family who hold shares, etc).With SRTT under a regulatory ban, the trusts which hold a majority stake cannot nominate anyone, and hence the roadblock that forced the adjournment remains.But any Tata Sons shareholder, holding even one share, can now move National Company Law Tribunal, seeking a court-ordered AGM under Section 97 of the Companies Act that would override the company's quorum requirement. The move need not even wait on Tata Sons fixing a new date, or on a second AGM failing for want of quorum.But even a court-directed meeting would not change the arithmetic. Chandrasekaran's reappointment as director needs a majority of votes cast in favour.Unlike the quorum requirement, there is no Articles provision requiring SDTT and SRTT to vote jointly. SDTT and other Tata Trusts entities, holding about 42% of Tata Sons, are expected to vote against. SRTT, at 24%, cannot vote as Maharashtra charity commissioner's restrictions bar it from holding board meetings, and hence also from deciding how to vote.The Shapoorji Pallonji Group, at 18%, is expected to back the resolution or abstain. How Tata group companies, holding about 13%, will vote is unclear, given Chandrasekaran chairs several of them. Trusts have discounted the Tata companies bloc in their reckoning, nor do they expect Shapoorji Pallonji's support. Even if both groups vote in favour, they fall well short of Trusts' 42% against, given a scenario where only 76% of votes are cast.Whatever Shapoorji Pallonji or the Tata companies decide, Chandrasekaran's fate rests with the Trusts bloc led by Noel Tata.
Article Summary: Tata Sons has to decide on a new AGM date as the Aug meeting was adjourned for want of quorum. If Chandrasekaran succeeds in winning reappointment as director, the chairmanship extends to Feb 21, 2032. Failure to do so, and his term at Tata Sons ends immediately.

Article Title: Commissions capped as fees soar 4x faster than premium; regulator seeks to limit distribution costs and misselling
Article Text:
Representative AI image

MUMBAI: The insurance regulator has sought to curb distribution costs and misselling by tightening limits on commissions and other expenses, after a reform meant to give insurers greater flexibility instead resulted in a big chunk of premium income being gobbled up by distributors.The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Irdai), in a consultation paper, has proposed reducing the segment-level cap on expenses of management (EoM) for general insurers from 30% to 20% over five years. For life insurers, the cap is proposed to fall to 10% over the same period.Irdai had replaced individual commission sub-caps with an overall, board-approved EoM limit in 2023, allowing insurers greater freedom to determine how they spent on distribution. The aim was to encourage competition and efficiency.The regulator now says the reform produced an unintended result. Insurers competed aggressively for access to intermediaries, pushing up distributor remuneration rather than passing efficiency gains to policyholders.Between FY23 and FY25, distributor remuneration grew four to five times faster than gross premium, according to Irdai. A larger share of premium income was therefore absorbed by commissions and other distribution payments making insurance less affordable and reducing returns for policyholders.Between FY23 and FY25 distributor payouts in general insurance rose 82% to Rs 24,400 crore, against 24-26% growth in premium, while first-year payouts in life insurance increased 48-52%, compared with 11-12% growth in premiums. Commission and fee income at brokers rose 60-75% over three years, while banks and corporate agents, which generated 24-28% of new business, captured 38-45% of incremental commissions after the 2023 deregulation.The regulator has also identified regulatory arbitrage among intermediary structures. Payments described as advertising, infrastructure or marketing fees, for instance, were being used to circumvent commission limits. Motor insurance illustrates the problem. Multilayered brokerage arrangements have contributed to high acquisition costs, including for mandatory motor third-party cover.Irdai also sees a link between high upfront commissions and policy churn and misselling, which can weaken policy persistency. Its proposals seek to standardise commissions according to product complexity and improve transparency in pricing and distribution payments.The proposed framework would also shift the basis for calculating EoM for general insurers from gross written premium to gross direct premium income in India, excluding inward reinsurance to avoid double-counting.The regulator’s wider objective is to reduce distribution costs while making insurance more accessible. The proposals include measures to lower entry and capital barriers for distributors.
Article Summary: Insurance regulator seeks to curb distribution costs and misselling. Reform meant to give insurers greater flexibility instead resulted in a big chunk of premium income being gobbled up by distributors. Irdai proposes reducing the segment-level cap on expenses of management (EoM) for general insurers from 30% to 20%.

Article Title: Trump buys up to $50,000 of Musk’s SpaceX, sells some a week later
Article Text:
Trump buys up to $50,000 of Musk’s SpaceX, sells some a week later

Trump’s investments in Musk’s companies

Microsoft, Amazon among major July trades

Stocks, ETFs and bonds

Trading activity remains high

US President Donald Trump has continued to bet on Elon Musk’s aerospace giant SpaceX, buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of the firm’s shares back in July. The transactions were part of a busy month for Trump’s portfolio, which saw 1,156 purchases and sales disclosed in July.According to a public financial disclosure, Trump made the purchase on July 10 and sold some of the shares a week later, on July 17. The SpaceX trades add to Trump’s investment activity involving Elon Musk’s companies, as he also bought and sold Tesla shares during the period.The combined value of those transactions was between roughly $79 million and $270 million, according to an estimation by CNBC. Of the total amount, purchases totalled at least $43.6 million, while sales amounted to at least $35.6 million.Trump had already reported buying between $15,001 and $50,000 worth of SpaceX shares on June 23. SpaceX went public on June 12 in the largest US IPO on record, with the space, satellite and AI provider valued at $1.77 trillion.SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider. It also owns Musk’s xAI, which has a Pentagon contract worth up to $200 million.Musk was Trump’s biggest financial backer in 2024 and later served as an adviser to his administration.Trump also traded Tesla shares several times. He bought between $100,001 and $250,000 of Tesla on June 15 and between $15,001 and $50,000 the following day. He then sold between $131,004 and $365,000 across four transactions before buying another $100,001 to $250,000 of the automaker’s shares on July 27.Trump’s July trading extended well beyond Musk’s companies, with Microsoft and Amazon among the biggest transactions.On July 20, he sold between $5 million and $25 million worth of shares in each company. Three days later, he bought between $100,001 and $250,000 of Microsoft and between $1,001 and $15,000 of Amazon.The same July 20 filing showed Trump selling between $1 million and $5 million of Oracle and buying between $500,001 and $1 million of Nvidia.He also sold between $250,001 and $500,000 of Northrop Grumman shares that day. The trade took place on the same day Trump signed an executive order tightening supply chain requirements for defence contractors and restricting waivers for certain critical materials sourced from China and other covered countries. The disclosure does not show when the trade took place or who made the investment decision.The July disclosure also shows Trump buying between $1 million and $5 million each of Intuit, Marvell Technology, Salesforce and Church & Dwight. He bought between $250,000 and $500,000 of Axon Enterprises, which works frequently with Immigration and Customs Enforcement.Trump also moved money across exchange-traded funds. On July 8, he bought between $1 million and $5 million each of the State Street SPDR Bloomberg International Treasury Bond ETF, Fidelity MSCI Communication Services Index ETF, Vanguard Short-Term Bond Index Fund ETF and Vanguard Dividend Appreciation Index Fund ETF.On the same day, he sold between $1 million and $5 million each of the iShares US Treasury Bond ETF, State Street Communication Services Select Sector SPDR ETF and iShares International Treasury Bond ETF.Ten-year yields climbed on July 8, led by soaring oil prices, after Trump said at the NATO summit in Turkey that he thought a ceasefire with Iran was over.The filing also showed several large purchases of municipal and other bonds, including between $1 million and $5 million each of two Miami-Dade County, Florida, aviation revenue bonds, a St Louis County, Missouri, school district bond and a Main Street Natural Gas bond.The July disclosure follows another heavy month of trading in June, when Trump reported 1,051 transactions worth between $78.1 million and $263.1 million across stocks, bonds and ETFs.His 2025 annual financial disclosure showed more than 21,000 securities trades across eight accounts holding at least $858 million. That compared with 86 stock transactions disclosed during his first year in office in 2017.The White House has repeatedly said Trump’s portfolio is managed independently and that neither he nor his family has a role in investment decisions.“President Trump’s stock and bond portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle said in response to CNBC’s questions about Trump’s latest disclosure.“Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold.”
Article Summary: Trump bought up to $50,000 of SpaceX shares on July 10. He then sold some of the shares a week later, on July 17. SpaceX went public on June 12 in the largest US IPO on record. Trump also bought and sold Tesla shares during the period. Microsoft and Amazon among the biggest transactions.

Article Title: 'Bigger deal' on table: US, China extend trade truce by two months as Xi visits Washington
Article Text:
File photo: US president Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping participate in an arrival ceremony at Joint Base Andrews, Md. (AP Photo)

A truce, but plenty left to settle

Trade is only one piece of the Trump-Xi agenda

The United States and China have agreed to extend their trade truce by two months, giving US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping more time to manage their wider economic rivalry. This truce extension comes as Xi begins his three-day state visit to Washington.US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said the extension would keep the agreement in place until January 10, moving the deadline beyond its original November 10 expiry. The announcement came hours after Bessent held an unscheduled meeting with Chinese vice-premier He Lifeng in Washington.Bessent said the two sides had agreed to extend what Washington calls the “Busan Agreement” while they assess whether Beijing is delivering on its commitments. He said some Chinese commitments, particularly on rare-earth exports, had not been fully met and that the additional time would allow Washington to judge progress.The extension also followed renewed discussions about a potentially broader trade agreement. Bessent said China had proposed a “bigger deal”, while the two sides had already agreed to launch an AI dialogue and establish a bilateral trade body during their earlier talks.The truce itself had helped pull US and China back from the brink after Trump's sweeping tariffs triggered a major trade confrontation. Under the Busan agreement, the two sides lowered some tariffs, paused additional restrictions and rare-earth export controls, and secured Chinese commitments on US soybeans and fentanyl precursors.Also read | 100-foot-long red carpet and B-1 bombers: How Trump welcomed Xi to US The leaders' talks today are expected to cover Taiwan, technology, artificial intelligence and China's relationship with Iran alongside trade. Reuters reported that Xi was likely to press Beijing's position on Taiwan, including its objections to US arms sales, while Trump was expected to maintain US export controls.AI is emerging as another area where the two rivals may try to keep communication open despite fierce technological competition. Bessent said Washington and Beijing were working to define risks including uncontrolled AI agents and non-state actors using AI for cyber operations or biological threats. A further meeting on AI safety is expected in Shenzhen in about two months.The immediate outcome of these meetings is more likely to be a series of narrower agreements that keep the relationship stable while leaving the deeper disputes over trade, technology, Taiwan and Iran unresolved.
Article Summary: US treasury secretary Scott Bessent said the extension would keep the agreement in place until January 10. The extension also followed renewed discussions about a potentially broader trade agreement. The leaders' talks today are expected to cover Taiwan, technology, artificial intelligence and China's relationship with Iran alongside trade.

Article Title: Trump weighs 90-day diesel export ban as US fuel prices hit record high: Report
Article Text:
The proposed ban comes as diesel prices have surged amid disruptions linked to the Trump administration's war against Iran, which began in February, and Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Farm-state Republicans have been pressing the administration to act as fuel costs rise.

Trump weighs ban despite opposition

Officials divided over proposal

White House rejects report

Political pressure grows

The Trump administration is preparing a 90-day ban on US diesel exports in an effort to bring down soaring energy prices ahead of the midterm elections, Politico reported on Wednesday, citing five people familiar with the discussions. President Donald Trump is inclined to announce the restriction by the end of the week, even as the proposal faces opposition inside the administration and from the oil industry.US ultra low-sulfur diesel futures fell more than 5 per cent after the report. The October futures contract was trading at $4.7199 a gallon, down 4.5 per cent.The proposed ban comes as diesel prices have surged amid disruptions linked to the Trump administration's war against Iran, which began in February, and Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Farm-state Republicans have been pressing the administration to act as fuel costs rise.The average US diesel price reached $6.52 a gallon on Wednesday, according to AAA. That was 91 cents higher than a month earlier and $2.83 higher than a year ago.The legal process for imposing a 90-day restriction is still being worked out, according to people familiar with the discussions. If implemented, it would be the first restriction on US energy exports since the Obama administration lifted the country's decades-old ban on crude oil exports in 2015.Some Republican lawmakers, refining industry executives and administration officials have argued against a complete ban. They have warned that any short-term fall in diesel prices could eventually be followed by higher prices for diesel, petrol, jet fuel and other fuels.A temporary export halt could initially increase domestic diesel supplies. Fuel shipments originally bound for Europe or Asia could instead be directed into the US market, potentially pushing prices down in some regions.But refiners could later respond by cutting production because of the loss of a major export market. That could reduce domestic supplies and push prices higher, according to people familiar with the discussions.US energy secretary Chris Wright, treasury secretary Scott Bessent and interior secretary Doug Burgum have protested against a total ban, people familiar with the internal discussions said.Wright also spoke to energy company executives on Tuesday night and told them that a 90-day ban was likely to be announced in the coming days, according to a Trump energy adviser. Several executives then contacted the White House to oppose the proposal.The adviser said there was still uncertainty over whether the plan would go ahead, warning that “there’s a lot of swirl so it might change.”“It’s a terrible idea,” the adviser said.Another industry official said the final decision could depend on the “last person in the room” with Trump before he makes a decision.Wright later spoke against the proposal at an event in New York on Wednesday.The White House and energy department did not immediately address specific questions about the reported plan.A White House official rejected the Politico report, saying: “This is another fake news news story from Politico.”An external adviser to the administration said there had been “a bunch of frantic outreach” in recent days to find alternatives to an export ban.The adviser said there were concerns that the administration could repeatedly extend a temporary ban, creating a precedent for greater government intervention in energy markets.“It’s clear that there is a lot of internal opposition to it,” the person said.The reported proposal comes less than seven weeks before the US midterm elections, with Republican candidates facing pressure over high energy costs.One oil industry executive who has discussed the proposal with senior White House officials said Trump was inclined to announce the ban by the end of the week and view any negative consequences as “a December problem”.Another person familiar with the White House discussions said the pressure to act on fuel prices had overtaken concerns about the potential consequences.“What has overpowered cooler heads [in the White House] is the absolutely, sky-is-falling, we-have-to-do-something concern about prices at the pump” faction, the person said. “That camp has been swept aside by the political camp, which says, ‘dammit, something has to happen.’”
Article Summary: The proposed ban comes as diesel prices have surged amid disruptions linked to the Trump administration's war against Iran. Farm-state Republicans have been pressing the administration to act as fuel costs rise. If implemented, it would be the first restriction on US energy exports since the Obama administration lifted the country's decades-old ban on crude oil exports.

Article Title: Russian oligarch’s wedding gift to Trump Jr puts family dealings under scrutiny
Article Text:
Russian oligarch’s wedding gift for Trump Jr puts family dealings under scrutiny

Curtis seeks scrutiny of Jr's foreign ties

Russian oligarch helped fund wedding celebrations

More facts needed

A Russian oligarch’s role in Donald Trump Jr’s wedding celebrations has now sparked a call for a Senate investigation from the GOP. Republican senator John Curtis of Utah has asked the Judiciary Committee to examine whether US president Donald Trump’s son benefited financially from his proximity to the White House.Curtis, who is not a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, made the request in a letter sent on Tuesday to committee chairman Chuck Grassley, a Republican from Iowa, and the panel’s top Democrat, Illinois Senator Dick Durbin. He asked the committee to subpoena Trump Jr over his business dealings, relationships with foreign individuals and entities, gifts and other benefits he has received, and any instances in which his relationship with President Donald Trump “was invoked or understood to provide value. ”Curtis also called for the same scrutiny of Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden.“The country should not have to accept one standard for the family of a Republican president and another for the family of a Democratic president,” Curtis wrote.The request puts a Republican senator at the centre of scrutiny of Trump’s family at a time when most Republican lawmakers have largely avoided weighing in on the president’s son.Curtis, who was first elected to the Senate in 2024, has previously vowed not to shy away from disagreements with Trump. He has publicly broken with the president several times, including rejecting Trump’s calls to eliminate the Senate filibuster.His latest criticism, however, goes beyond a disagreement over policy. Curtis last Friday described the reported wedding funding as “corruption” and said he would say more about the issue in the coming days.“A Russian oligarch paid for a lavish wedding after-party for Donald Trump Jr, which to me just stinks. It’s corruption. I don’t like it,” Curtis said in a video posted on social media.Earlier on Tuesday, Curtis also referred to the Republican-led scrutiny of Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships, writing that Republicans “nearly wore out the subpoena machine investigating Hunter Biden’s foreign relationships” and that they “should not unplug it now.”The controversy follows a report by ProPublica last week that Umar Kremlev, who has close ties to Russian President Vladimir Putin, helped pay for the rental of a private island and a fireworks show during celebrations for Trump Jr and socialite Bettina Anderson’s wedding in the Bahamas in May.Bettina Trump later addressed Kremlev’s involvement in an Instagram post signed by the couple. She described Kremlev, who is head of the International Boxing Association, as a “dear friend” who “very generously hosted two incredible nights of celebrations for us AFTER our wedding.”Though Trump did not attend his son’s wedding, he defended Kremlev’s involvement but said the money would be paid back.Curtis’ letter asks the Judiciary Committee to examine Trump Jr’s business dealings, his relationships with foreign individuals and entities, and gifts or other benefits he has received. It also seeks scrutiny of instances in which his relationship with the president “was invoked or understood to provide value.”Grassley has not yet committed to an investigation. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, he said he was not yet familiar with the facts surrounding the case and would need to gather more information before deciding what action to take.“I’m going to take these requests seriously and sit down with staff and see what we can do,” Grassley said.He added that the process would take time and said, “it takes time, and if you were going to ask me when we're going to have a hearing, there’s no way I could answer that today.”Senate majority leader John Thune, Republican of South Dakota, also declined to offer a view, saying he did not “have an observation on that.”Still, some Republican lawmakers have indicated that they would support Curtis’ request.The developments come as a few Republicans have recently shown a greater willingness to criticise Trump’s policies after largely avoiding public breaks with him during much of his second term.Meanwhile, the ongoing war in Iran, high gas prices and mounting concerns about Republican prospects in November’s midterm elections have brought increased scrutiny of the president from within his own party.
Article Summary: Republican senator John Curtis of Utah has asked the Judiciary Committee to examine whether US president Donald Trump’s son benefited financially from his proximity to the White House. Curtis also called for the same scrutiny of Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden.

Article Title: Oil prices ease as Saudi Arabia restores key pipeline, traders remain optimistic on US-Iran talks
Article Text:
Oil prices ease below $100 per barrel

Oil prices slipped below the $100-a-barrel mark on Wednesday as Saudi Arabia began restoring crude supplies through a key pipeline to the Red Sea, while hopes of a diplomatic breakthrough in the US-Iran war added to the ease.WTI crude was trading at $90.10 a barrel, down 42 cents, or 0.46%, while Brent crude stood at $99.09, down 16 cents, or 0.16% around 7:30 am IST.The decline came after Brent closed below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8. Expectations of improving oil supplies, along with efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the nearly seven-month conflict, put pressure on benchmark crude prices.US President Donald Trump has warned that he could "annihilate" Iran, but also said his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held productive talks with Iranian mediators aimed at ending the war."I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal," Trump said.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia has restarted operations on its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea, according to three sources briefed on the matter. The move has been accompanied by signs of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.The pipeline had been shut on September 11 after drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia blamed on an Iraqi militia, halted crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and other Gulf producers through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been using the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels of crude per day to Yanbu. That volume is equivalent to around 4% of global oil supply.Iraq is also increasing its oil exports. Oil minister Basim Mohammed said on Tuesday that the country was exporting more than 3 million barrels per day and expected exports through Turkey to rise to more than 600,000 bpd.Provisional figures from shiptracking firms Vortexa and Kpler put Iraq's crude exports in August at 2.3 million bpd and 2.17 million bpd, respectively. Both estimates were higher than July levels but remained below the February pre-war levels of 3.7 million bpd and 3.362 million bpd, respectively.Adding to the pressure on oil prices, industry data showed US crude inventories increased by 1.8 million barrels in the week to September 18. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected inventories to decline.As the conflict continues for over 6 months now, oil markets have continued to remain volatile as global supply chains continue to face disruption.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $90.10 a barrel, down 42 cents, or 0.46%, while Brent crude stood at $99.09. The decline came after Brent closed below $100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8.

Article Title: UNGA address: Donald Trump touts Venezuela oil deal, says it will drive down energy prices worldwide
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump addresses the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) at the UN Headquarters, in New York, USA

Trump highlights 65 billion barrels of oil

Venezuela deal expected to boost oil production

Trump links Venezuela policy to wider US interests

Trump expects Iran deal after US midterm election

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday said the oil deal between the United States and Venezuela will help drive down energy costs around the world, describing it as the "largest oil deal in history" and saying it covers 65 billion barrels of oil.Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Trump said the agreement would benefit both Venezuela and the US, while adding that major global oil companies were entering Venezuela."The biggest oil companies in the world are going in [to Venezuela], and the numbers are absolutely incredible," Trump said.Trump said the US and Venezuela had signed an agreement covering 65 billion barrels of oil, which he said would "benefit both Venezuela and the United States enormously and help drive down the cost of energy all over the world".He also said the two countries together "have more than 60% of the oil in the world".The deal centres on Venezuela's vast oil reserves and efforts to revive its oil industry.Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has said the agreement aims to increase the country's oil production to 1.5 million barrels per day.The deal covers 17 oil fields with a proven potential of 65 billion barrels, according to Rodriguez's statement cited in the background copy.It could bring $100 billion in investment into Venezuela's oil industry and generate more than $209 billion in taxes for Caracas.The US government and an unnamed private operator in Venezuela have set up a new company with rights to untapped oil fields for 100 years, according to the background information.The US is expected to receive 55% of the new company's effective output through an ownership stake and the right to buy oil at cost. A US official said oil bought by the US would go towards its strategic oil reserves and the military.However, Venezuela's oil infrastructure is in poor condition and would require years and billions of dollars in investment to repair.Trump has said the agreement will help lower gasoline prices in the US. But experts believe Venezuelan oil production was unlikely to increase quickly.Amy Myers Jaffe of New York University said the deal could be helpful in the long run but would not immediately change retail gasoline prices. Kevin Book of ClearView Energy Partners said increasing production would take many years because of the scale of investment required.Trump also highlighted the US military operation in January to arrest then-President Nicolás Maduro."Since that day, hundreds of Venezuelan political prisoners have been freed. They’ve let them out of jails, and we’re working closely with the leaders of Venezuela to forge a much better future for the Venezuelan people," Trump said."Our actions in Venezuela are proof that the United States will no longer permit threats to America to gain a foothold anywhere in the Western Hemisphere," he added.The oil agreement has also faced criticism in Venezuela. Harvard University professor and former Venezuelan planning minister Ricardo Hausmann called it a "shameful deal", while criticising the agreement's legitimacy.In his UN remarks, Trump also said he believed the US would reach a deal with Iran after the November 3 midterm elections."I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," Trump said, according to Reuters.Trump also raised the possibility of either reaching an agreement with Iran or taking military action, saying he had "a big decision to make".
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump said the oil deal between the United States and Venezuela will help drive down energy costs around the world. He said the agreement would benefit both Venezuela and the US, while adding that major global oil companies were entering Venezuela. Trump also said he believed the US would reach a deal with Iran after the November 3 midterm elections.

Article Title: Diesel prices hit records as Iran, Ukraine wars disrupt fuel supplies
Article Text:
A price board at a petrol station in Paris, France (Picture credit: Reuters)

Refinery disruptions deepen global diesel squeeze

Russia's refinery attacks hit diesel exports

US diesel stocks remain below seasonal levels

Asia prices remain near record levels

Few quick options to ease fuel prices

Diesel prices have surged to record levels in Europe and the United States as wars in Iran and Ukraine disrupt supplies from major producers and damage refineries, leaving limited options to prevent further gains.European diesel futures closed at an all-time high last week, having more than doubled from the start of 2026. Supply disruptions have also spread to the Red Sea, where Saudi Arabia loads most of its diesel.In the US, average retail diesel prices crossed $6 a gallon for the first time on record this month. In Asia, benchmark diesel prices have also remained close to record levels amid disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian supplies.The wars in the Middle East and Ukraine have damaged refineries, while facilities elsewhere have been operating at high levels to make up for lost fuel supplies.US refineries were running at their highest level in eight years in late August, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA)."A key issue is that many refineries around the world are already stretched to capacity," the IEA said in a newsletter on Monday."This leaves few available options to prevent a further tightening of supplies and higher prices in the coming months."Middle East diesel exports fell by half between March and August compared with a year earlier, averaging 800,000 barrels per day, according to shipping data from Kpler. The region supplied nearly 41% of Europe's diesel imports in 2025."Any further disruption to Red Sea flows risks tightening an already stretched global diesel market," Kpler analyst George Shaw said, as cited by Reuters.Shaw added that refining capacity remained a key constraint.Russia, the world's second-largest diesel exporter after the US, banned diesel exports in July after Ukrainian drone attacks reduced refinery production.Russia and Ukraine have continued attacking each other's energy infrastructure despite an announcement by US President Donald Trump last week that they had agreed to stop. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday that he would meet Trump in the coming days.Russia had supplied significant volumes of diesel to countries including Turkey and Brazil before the ban, prompting importers to seek alternative supplies.In Europe, diesel stocks at the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp refining and storage hub were at their lowest level for this time of year on September 10, according to Insights Global.US diesel inventories also remain below normal seasonal levels despite high refinery utilisation. Stocks rose by about 600,000 barrels last week but stood at 96.97 million barrels, nearly 15% below the five-year average for the second week of September.Average US diesel prices reached a record $6.52 per gallon on Monday, according to the AAA Automobile Association.In France, the average diesel price reached a record €2.41 per litre on Sunday, according to an AFP analysis.Asian diesel prices have also risen sharply because of disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian supplies. The benchmark diesel swaps price had eased from a March record of more than $200 a barrel but remained around $180 a barrel on September 18.Current levels are still about twice their pre-war values.China's diesel exports fell 26% in April-June from a year earlier after the government limited refined-product exports, tightening global supplies.Exports subsequently recovered to around 320,000 barrels per day in August, their highest level in nearly 2.5 years, while domestic stocks declined.The disruptions have created limited short-term options for increasing diesel supplies. Rystad Energy vice-president Janiv Shah said some unused refining capacity existed on paper but that little could be activated quickly and supplied with the appropriate crude.A resumption of oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz would likely be the quickest way to ease prices, Shah said, as it would allow Asian refineries to receive supplies.IEA oil industry and markets division head Toril Bosoni warned that if Gulf supplies remained constrained and commercial inventories continued to fall rapidly, higher prices and further reductions in demand could be needed to close the supply-demand gap.Shah said higher prices could reduce diesel consumption, but the short-term effect would be limited because trucking, agriculture, construction and industry have few immediate alternatives.
Article Summary: European diesel futures closed at an all-time high last week, having more than doubled from the start of 2026. In the US, average retail diesel prices crossed $6 a gallon for the first time on record this month. In Asia, benchmark diesel prices have also remained close to record levels amid disruptions to Middle Eastern and Russian supplies.

Article Title: From Russian oil to Belarusian potash, more hypocrisy from Washington
Article Text:
Trump administration faces flak from critics over Belarus potash deal amid pressure on India over Russian energy

TOI correspondent from Washington:

Critics are calling out the Trump administration for hypocrisy and double standards after MAGA supremo Donald Trump announced a potash (fertiliser) deal on Monday with Belarus, a close ally of Moscow, days after he signed a bill which would punish India if it buys Russian energy.Arising from his spat with Canada, which supplies 85 per cent of US-needed potash, a key farming input, Trump announced with his customary fanfare that Washington is working on a “massive Deal” to purchase potash from Belarus at prices “substantially less” than what Washington currently pays Ottawa, calling it good news for American farmers. The move will affect New Delhi because Belarus is also an established supplier of potash to the Indian agricultural market.The apparent double standard is already drawing flak in diplomatic circles.
